Platelet defect, immunodeficiency and severe neurologic impairment; pulmonary interstitial abnormalities in 1/1; ocular and cutaneous albinism omitted because of the cap.

A sleep-wake disorder defined by pathological excessive sleepiness.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; an underlying structural CNS lesion is not established by this concept.
Hereditary erythrocyte membrane phospholipid abnormality causing hemolysis; jaundice reflects red-cell destruction rather than liver damage.

Olivopontocerebellar degeneration and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; optic atrophy and coloboma occur in only 5-29%.
Epidermal keratinization disorder causing blistering, ichthyosis and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis.
Cerebellar ataxia and sensory neuropathy define SCA18; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Weakness and pes cavus accompany neuropathy; muscle atrophy is only 5-29%.
Skin dysplasia defines FFDD4. Despite the isolated-skin definition, supplied HPO reports buccal anomalies in 80-99%, cleft palate and CNS hemorrhage/hydrocephalus in 30-79%.

Explicitly nonsyndromic CRYAB-related cataract; the broader gene-associated myopathy and cardiomyopathy spectrum does not apply.
Inherited hepatic porphyrin metabolism disorder with photosensitive skin fragility and blistering; cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma are separate complications.
Subaortic fibrous obstruction impairs left ventricular outflow.
Retinal degeneration and ataxia in most patients are explicitly defining manifestations.
Benign perineurial tumor arising within a peripheral nerve; associated weakness reflects nerve injury.
Defined by reduced mature circulating granulocytes; infection risk does not establish an additional affected organ.
Neurodevelopmental disease with neuropathy; optic atrophy 3/8, myopia 4/8 and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 3/8. Amyotrophy may be neurogenic; lactate alone adds no axis.
